_comment: Mutation sweep for V-CTR-021 -- the two path dialects of 06 §4.2 are never interchangeable. Run: python3 dev/mutate.py verification/mutants/V-CTR-021.json. Every row names the test that must fail; see dev/mutate.py for why rc != 0 is not a catch. Both packages are swept together because the property spans them: the predicate lives in `classify`, the enforcement point the requirement names is `ChangePolicy` admission in `webhook`, the rule validator refuses a second time, and the matcher's own refusal is the reason a path that got past all three still cannot silently match. A sweep of one package alone would score green while a layer in the other was gone.

mutants.why: THE defect the clause exists for. `/spec/replicas` is a WELL-FORMED dotted path whose single segment is literally named `/spec/replicas`, so with the guard gone it admits, stores, lists -- and matches nothing, forever. A gate that has silently stopped gating is indistinguishable from a gate with nothing to catch.

The predicate survives and the requirement's named enforcement point stops calling it. `ValidateChangeRule` still refuses the rule, so the policy is still rejected -- which is why this has to be caught on the FIELD PATH and not on the refusal: the author is told rules[0] is wrong and not which of its paths.

06 §4.2 specifies the wording, and it specifies it because the mistake is silent: the message is the entire user-facing explanation of a dialect confusion. A paraphrase is a spec drift no compiler and no schema can see.

edits.find: return fmt.Errorf("expected a dotted field path, not a JSON Pointer")
edits.replace: return fmt.Errorf("field paths must be dotted, not JSON Pointers")

mutants.why: `when.fieldPaths` is a list. Reporting against the rule tells an author with six paths that one of them is a Pointer, and 06 §4.2's whole argument is that the reader cannot see which -- the two dialects look alike, which is how the entry got written. Two edits, because dropping the index alone leaves `j` unused and Go refuses to compile it -- a BROKEN row measures nothing (LSN-048).

The rule-level validator refuses the same path. With the dedup guard gone the author reads two errors for one mistake, goes looking for a second problem, and discounts the specific field-level message as a restatement of the generic one.

The second of the two refusals admission performs, and the one nothing user-facing would notice going: with the webhook's own loop intact a policy author sees the same single error, so only a test aimed at `ValidateChangeRule` can see this. It is also the layer a direct write or a pre-webhook object reaches.

The other direction, and the most plausible defect in the set: be liberal in what you accept. Translating `/spec/replicas` into `spec.replicas` at match time makes the dialects interchangeable exactly where 06 §4.2 says they never are -- and it makes every rejection above look like pedantry, which is how they get removed next.
